Hi Evan / Sarah —

Great questions — short answers first, then a little more detail and action items.

1) Billing model: Yes — Redwood supports standard AWS Marketplace SaaS metering (AWS invoices the customer). In that flow, Redwood reports usage via AWS APIs (PutUsageRecords) and AWS handles buyer billing and settlement.

2) Reconciliation exports: We provide both: (a) we push usage to AWS; (b) Redwood can produce a daily reconciliation ledger (CSV) with canonical mapping between your customer ids and AWS ResourceId (entitlement_id). We recommend you wire that ledger into your ingestion pipeline; sample CSV schema is in the attached spec.

3) Regional endpoints & SLA: Redwood will host a fulfillment endpoint in us-east-1 by default. We can configure a secondary endpoint in us-west-2 for failover and enable automatic routing. SLA options (99.9 vs 99.95) depend on whether you want Reserved capacity (Dedicated) for guaranteed throughput — we can include a pricing addendum in the SOW.

Technical notes & proposed ingestion pattern:
- Real-time: use AWS Marketplace reporting + Redwood webhook for near-real-time reconciliation.
- Batch: Redwood can accept daily batched S3 uploads for high-cardinality datasets and ingest them into the reconciliation ledger.
- Entitlement mapping: provide a mapping file (CSV) with columns: nova_customer_id, aws_entitlement_id, sku, billing_dimension.

Action items (updated):
- Evan: confirm buyer-billed Marketplace by 2025-05-06 (ok if you already did).
- Sarah: send SOC2 contact + vendor questionnaire answers by 2025-05-07.
- NovaMed engineering: share sample customer id map and desired billing granularity by 2025-05-09.
- Redwood (Aditya): will share sample PutUsageRecords payloads and a test account by 2025-05-08.

DocuSign / SOW: Monica will prepare SOW v1 and share a DocuSign route once we confirm the billing model. Draft SOW attached (NovaMed_SOW_v1.docx).

"nova-123, entitlement-aws-xyz, sku:RED-ML-API, per-request"

Happy to take 30 minutes next week to walk the engineering team through the webhook and reconciliation flow.

Thanks,

Subject: Technical payloads: PutUsageRecords examples & idempotency guidance

Hi Evan / Sarah —

Aditya here (solutions eng) — looping in a few technical specifics so your engineering team can prototype. Below are minimal examples and operational notes.

Example PutUsageRecords payload (simplified):
- ResourceId: "entitlement-aws-xyz"  // maps to NovaMed customer id in our ledger
- Timestamp: 2025-05-06T08:00:00Z
- UsageDimension: "API-CALLS"
- Quantity: 12345
- Unit: "requests"

Notes / operational guidance:
- Idempotency: include a deterministic idempotency key per usage batch (sha256(customer_id + timestamp + dimension)).
- Batching: we recommend 100-1,000 records per batch depending on cardinality; smaller batches for low latency, larger for efficiency.
- Retries/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter; implement 429/5xx retries. Redwood will accept retries and dedupe by idempotency key on ingestion.
- Test environment: we'll provision a test AWS listing and provide credentials for a sandbox PutUsageRecords service.

Optional: if you want lower tail-latency for customer-facing activation (fast entitlement checks), we can enable prefix KV caching at the runtime and provide a per-customer cache TTL recommendation. That feature requires a short onboarding step in the Dedicated config if you go reserved.

Attachment (stub): metering-payload-examples.json (contains curl --data examples, sample JSON bodies, and recommended retry algorithm).

I'll be available for a technical walkthrough Wed/Thu this week — let me know a slot and we can share a screen and run a PutUsageRecords test live.

Regards,
